To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

adoptive immunotherapy of mice with advanced 4TIL tumors with bryostain and ionomycin activated TIL induces regression and that the predominant mediators of regression are CD8 T cells that are derived from CD62 Llow T cells, which proliferate vigorously in the tumor draining LNs, migrate to and/or proliferate in the tumor, and are activated in vivo.
adoptively transferred CD8 T cells are the mediators of tumor rejection, and that host T cells are unnecessary for tumor rejection.
the adoptively transferred T cells are the key to the anti-tumor response, and the host immune system is not required for the anti-tumor effects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how adoptive immunotherapy can be improved to induce regression of advanced tumors.
the development of an effective immunotherapy for breast cancer.
the development of novel approaches to the immunotherapy of breast cancer.

adoptively transferred T lymphocytes are the principal mediator of tumor regression in this model, and that cyclophosphamid pre-treatment auguments the anti-tumor effects.
adoptively transferred CD8 T cells are the mediators of tumor destruction, and the mechanism of tumor destruction involves the activation of endogenous T cells.

adoptively transferred tumor-draining lymph node lymphocytes are a heterogeneous population of cells that are activated ex vivo with bryostain and ionomycin and then transferred to tumor-bearing recipients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the anti-tumor effects of bryostatin/ionomycin activation and adoptive immunotherapy are mediated by a subset (CD8+) of the transferred lymphocytes.

adoptive transfer of tumor draining lymphocytes can be an effective therapy for advanced tumors, but the mechanism of tumor regression is complex, involving multiple cell subsets, and is not fully elucidated.

adoptively transferred T cells can be activated ex vivo to mediate the rejection of poorly immunogenic tumors, and that the mechanism involves a subset of T cells which proliferate and infiltrate the tumor and tumor draining lymph nodes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
adoptive transfer of tumor draining lymph node cells activated with bryostatine and ionomycin is a promising immunotherapy for advanced tumors.
